newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo '96 industry output put at 6.5 pct - institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo '96 industry output put at 6.5 pct - institute.

text.p: Yugoslav annual industrial growth could reach 6.5 percent by year-end, analysts of the Belgrade Economics Institute forecast on Tuesday.

"After a slight drop of 3.1 percent in July on June, industrial output resumed growth in August so that our earlier forecast for the year has been revised upwards," said Miroljub Labus, an economist with the institute.
The forecast is more than double previous forecasts, which put annual growth for 1996 near three percent.
Although output in the third quarter tends to decline, this did not happen because new industrial capacities reopened, especially in Montenegro, Labus said.
He said a 2.1-percent August increase over July indicated production in the third quarter was reviving, especially in the power, chemicals and non-metals industries.
But this growth was primarily attributable to increased energy production and good results from Montenegro's industry, Labus said.
"Practically, Serbian industry output remained unchanged at the July level, while Montenegrin output rose as much as 40 percent in August, raising the overall result," he said.
According to official statistics, August output was 9.7 percent up on the same month in 1995, before sanctions against rump Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were suspended last November.
The average monthly growth in the first eight months was 4.8 percent compared to the same period last year.
Output tends to increase in the fourth quarter mainly due to higher power production. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
